chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

"If he performs i'tikaf for one day, even if he did not specify a condition, he has the right to exit and break his i'tikaf. And if he stays for two days and did not specify a condition, he does not have the right to exit and break his i'tikaf until three days have passed."
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And i'tikaf is not valid except in the Greatest Mosque.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for breaking i'tikaf if no specific duration was pledged?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key jurisprudential distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the binding nature of i'tikaf based on duration: a single day is revocable, while two days require completion of the third, reflecting the transition from a voluntary act to an obligatory vow. Al-Tusi’s commentary clarifies that this ruling applies specifically to the 'Greatest Mosque' (Al-Masjid al-Haram), highlighting the spatial sanctity associated with the primary form of i'tikaf. This rule underscores the principle that prolonged seclusion creates a stronger spiritual and legal commitment, preventing arbitrary abandonment of the worship.
